overview: The Medford School Committee is responsible for the policy, budget, and governance of the Medford Public Schools district. Over a four-year period from 2022 to 2026, the committee's work has been dominated by a multi-phase high school building project, district-wide infrastructure repairs, and the resolution of protracted labor negotiations. The body has also addressed student safety crises, elementary school overcrowding, and the adoption of modern academic policies for literacy and technology. As of late 2026, the committee has finalized permanent leadership, approved major geothermal and solar energy projects, and is moving toward the schematic design phase for a new comprehensive high school.

threads.name: Medford High School Building Project
threads.summary: Beginning with a 2022 Statement of Interest to the MSBA, the committee has progressed through eligibility and feasibility phases for a major high school renovation or replacement. Significant milestones included the 2023 acceptance into the MSBA core program, the 2024 formation of the Building Committee, and the 2026 narrowing of design options to a preferred alternative. The project must navigate complex constraints, including a 999-year DCR deed restriction on Edgley Field that forced the elimination of several building footprints. Recent work has focused on securing a LEED v4 Silver certification and integrating vocational and community-facing programs into the final design.

threads.name: HVAC and Accelerated Repair Infrastructure
threads.summary: Facing widespread cooling system failures across aging facilities, the committee initiated a series of large-scale infrastructure projects. In 2024, the body approved bonds totaling over $25 million for comprehensive HVAC replacements at the Andrews and McGlynn schools to address obsolete refrigerants and failed systems. Similar projects followed for the Brooks, Roberts, and Missituck schools, with the committee increasingly prioritizing decarbonization through geothermal heat pumps and solar power purchase agreements. The committee continues to manage a multi-year capital plan identifying over $80 million in priority maintenance needs.

threads.name: Labor Relations and Collective Bargaining
threads.summary: Labor negotiations were initially marked by a 2022 impasse with the Medford Teachers Association that required state mediation over disagreements regarding cost-of-living increases and scheduling. Between 2023 and 2025, the committee successfully ratified successor agreements for nearly all units, including teachers, paraprofessionals, nurses, custodians, and secretaries. A major three-year contract with the MTA was ratified in 2025, adding 15 minutes to the school day and reducing half-day schedules. Most recently, the committee approved a successor agreement with the Massachusetts Nurses Association running through 2028.

threads.name: District Leadership and Succession
threads.summary: The committee managed the leadership transition from long-serving Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent to her successor. Following Edouard-Vincent's 2024 departure, Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi was appointed as interim superintendent to ensure continuity during active MSBA and budget cycles. In early 2026, after a positive performance evaluation and a review of district stability, the committee voted to appoint Galusi as the permanent superintendent. The body subsequently approved a three-year contract for Galusi in May 2026.

threads.name: School Safety, Climate, and Bullying Prevention
threads.summary: Following a 2022 stabbing incident at the high school, the committee commissioned an independent security and climate review and implemented a 10-point safety plan involving bathroom monitoring and electronic hall passes. The body overhauled its Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan to ensure caregiver notification and language accessibility during investigations. Later efforts included the installation of vape detectors and security cameras across secondary schools and the adoption of a formal gender identity non-discrimination policy. The committee continues to monitor student disciplinary data and high school bathroom staffing to improve campus safety.

threads.name: Elementary Overcrowding and Redistricting
threads.summary: Critical overcrowding at Roberts Elementary School prompted the committee to investigate short-term and long-term space utilization strategies. Actions taken include the 2025 relocation of preschool classrooms to Missituck Elementary and the hiring of additional staff to manage high enrollment at the Roberts. The committee explored a proposal to restructure schools into K-4 and 5-8 configurations, but ultimately voted to delay any grade reconfiguration until 2028 to allow for further study. The body is currently drafting a formal intra-district enrollment policy to manage future reassignment requests.

threads.name: Academic Innovation and Technology Policy
threads.summary: The committee has overseen significant shifts in academic frameworks, including the adoption of the 'Into Reading' elementary literacy curriculum and a transition toward integrated mathematics pathways. In response to emerging technology, the body adopted a comprehensive policy in 2025 regulating the ethical use of generative artificial intelligence, later amending it to prohibit educators from using AI to grade qualitative student work. Other academic initiatives include the expansion of the Chapter 74 vocational programs and the implementation of a lottery-based admissions system for oversubscribed CTE pathways.

threads.name: Transportation Operations and Safety
threads.summary: The district has consistently faced operational challenges due to regional bus driver shortages, leading to route consolidations and overcrowded buses. In 2025, the committee approved a new five-year contract with Eastern Bus that included a preliminary phase for fleet electrification. To address safety concerns, the body authorized the use of paraprofessionals as bus monitors and passed a resolution requesting the city install automated stop-arm enforcement cameras. A new transportation manager was hired in 2026 to oversee logistics and improve communication with families.
